name: Jellyfin
description: Stream your movies, shows and music to any device. Uses the phone's hardware video encoder.
install:
apk add --no-cache jellyfin jellyfin-web
# Hardware encoding: Jellyfin's V4L2 option is routed to Android's MediaCodec by the
# ffmpeg shim. Only on first install, so a user's own choice is kept.
mkdir -p /var/lib/jellyfin/config
[ -e /var/lib/jellyfin/config/encoding.xml ] || cat > /var/lib/jellyfin/config/encoding.xml <<'XML'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<EncodingOptions xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
  <HardwareAccelerationType>v4l2m2m</HardwareAccelerationType>
  <EnableHardwareEncoding>true</EnableHardwareEncoding>
</EncodingOptions>
XML
# Torrent downloads show up in Jellyfin: a "Downloads" library (mixed movies and shows,
# watched for new files) once both apps are installed. Only once, so a user who
# removes the library in Jellyfin keeps it removed.
if [ -x /usr/bin/jellyfin ] && [ -x /usr/bin/qbittorrent-nox ] && [ ! -e /var/lib/jellyfin/.downloads-library ]; then
  mkdir -p /media/Downloads /var/lib/jellyfin/root/default/Downloads
  cd /var/lib/jellyfin/root/default/Downloads
  printf /media/Downloads > Downloads.mblink
  cat > options.xml <<'XML'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<LibraryOptions xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
  <Enabled>true</Enabled>
  <EnablePhotos>true</EnablePhotos>
  <EnableRealtimeMonitor>true</EnableRealtimeMonitor>
  <EnableLUFSScan>false</EnableLUFSScan>
  <EnableChapterImageExtraction>false</EnableChapterImageExtraction>
  <ExtractChapterImagesDuringLibraryScan>false</ExtractChapterImagesDuringLibraryScan>
  <EnableTrickplayImageExtraction>false</EnableTrickplayImageExtraction>
  <ExtractTrickplayImagesDuringLibraryScan>false</ExtractTrickplayImagesDuringLibraryScan>
  <PathInfos>
    <MediaPathInfo>
      <Path>/media/Downloads</Path>
    </MediaPathInfo>
  </PathInfos>
  <SaveLocalMetadata>false</SaveLocalMetadata>
  <EnableAutomaticSeriesGrouping>true</EnableAutomaticSeriesGrouping>
  <EnableEmbeddedTitles>false</EnableEmbeddedTitles>
  <EnableEmbeddedExtrasTitles>false</EnableEmbeddedExtrasTitles>
  <EnableEmbeddedEpisodeInfos>false</EnableEmbeddedEpisodeInfos>
  <AutomaticRefreshIntervalDays>0</AutomaticRefreshIntervalDays>
  <SeasonZeroDisplayName>Specials</SeasonZeroDisplayName>
  <DisabledLocalMetadataReaders />
  <DisabledSubtitleFetchers />
  <SubtitleFetcherOrder />
  <DisabledMediaSegmentProviders />
  <MediaSegmentProviderOrder />
  <SkipSubtitlesIfEmbeddedSubtitlesPresent>false</SkipSubtitlesIfEmbeddedSubtitlesPresent>
  <SkipSubtitlesIfAudioTrackMatches>true</SkipSubtitlesIfAudioTrackMatches>
  <RequirePerfectSubtitleMatch>true</RequirePerfectSubtitleMatch>
  <SaveSubtitlesWithMedia>true</SaveSubtitlesWithMedia>
  <DisabledLyricFetchers />
  <LyricFetcherOrder />
  <CustomTagDelimiters>
    <string>/</string>
    <string>|</string>
    <string>;</string>
    <string>\</string>
  </CustomTagDelimiters>
  <DelimiterWhitelist />
  <AutomaticallyAddToCollection>false</AutomaticallyAddToCollection>
  <AllowEmbeddedSubtitles>AllowAll</AllowEmbeddedSubtitles>
  <TypeOptions />
</LibraryOptions>
XML
  touch /var/lib/jellyfin/.downloads-library
fi
# Movies and Shows libraries when Radarr or Sonarr is installed (see media-stack).
[ ! -x /usr/local/lib/homedroid/media-stack ] || /usr/local/lib/homedroid/media-stack libraries

name: qBittorrent
description: Torrent client. Downloads go to the media library's Downloads folder, in order (stream while downloading), and keep seeding. Add from SSH: torrent 'magnet:?…'
install:
apk add --no-cache qbittorrent-nox curl jq
mkdir -p /media/Downloads /var/lib/qbittorrent/qBittorrent/config
# Only on first install, so the user's own settings are kept.
[ -e /var/lib/qbittorrent/qBittorrent/config/qBittorrent.conf ] || cat > /var/lib/qbittorrent/qBittorrent/config/qBittorrent.conf <<'CONF'
[LegalNotice]
Accepted=true

[BitTorrent]
Session\DefaultSavePath=/media/Downloads
Session\TempPathEnabled=false
Session\GlobalMaxRatio=-1
Session\GlobalMaxSeedingMinutes=-1
Session\QueueingSystemEnabled=false

[Preferences]
WebUI\Port=8081
WebUI\LocalHostAuth=false
CONF
cat > /usr/local/bin/torrent <<'SH'
#!/bin/sh
# torrent <magnet or .torrent URL>...   add, downloading pieces in order
# torrent list                          show progress
api=http://127.0.0.1:8081/api/v2
if ! curl -fsS -o /dev/null "$api/app/version" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo 'qBittorrent is not running: start the server in the Homedroid app.' >&2; exit 1
fi
case $1 in
''|-h|--help) sed -n '2,3s/^# //p' "$0"; exit 2 ;;
list) curl -fsS "$api/torrents/info" | jq -r '.[] | "\(.progress * 100 | floor)%\t\(.state)\t\(.name)"'; exit ;;
esac
for link do
  curl -fsS -F "urls=$link" -F sequentialDownload=true -F firstLastPiecePrio=true "$api/torrents/add" >/dev/null &&
    echo "Added: $link"
done
SH
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/torrent
# Torrent downloads show up in Jellyfin: a "Downloads" library (mixed movies and shows,
# watched for new files) once both apps are installed. Only once, so a user who
# removes the library in Jellyfin keeps it removed.
if [ -x /usr/bin/jellyfin ] && [ -x /usr/bin/qbittorrent-nox ] && [ ! -e /var/lib/jellyfin/.downloads-library ]; then
  mkdir -p /media/Downloads /var/lib/jellyfin/root/default/Downloads

  cat > options.xml <<'XML'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<LibraryOptions xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
  <Enabled>true</Enabled>
  <EnablePhotos>true</EnablePhotos>

  <EnableTrickplayImageExtraction>false</EnableTrickplayImageExtraction>
  <ExtractTrickplayImagesDuringLibraryScan>false</ExtractTrickplayImagesDuringLibraryScan>
  <PathInfos>
    <MediaPathInfo>
      <Path>/media/Downloads</Path>
    </MediaPathInfo>
  </PathInfos>
  <SaveLocalMetadata>false</SaveLocalMetadata>
  <EnableAutomaticSeriesGrouping>true</EnableAutomaticSeriesGrouping>
  <EnableEmbeddedTitles>false</EnableEmbeddedTitles>

    <string>/</string>

  <DelimiterWhitelist />

name: Prowlarr

name: Radarr
description: Finds, downloads and files movies for you. Sends downloads to qBittorrent and files finished movies in Movies, which Jellyfin shows as its own library.

name: Sonarr

name: Jellyseerr (Seerr)
description: A friendly page for finding movies and shows and asking for them; requests go to Radarr and Sonarr. Jellyseerr is now called Seerr. Sign in with your Jellyfin account; Radarr and Sonarr are added for you after that.

name: Home Assistant
description: Home automation hub. Network and cloud integrations work; USB radios and Bluetooth need root.
install:
apk add --no-cache python3 uv ffmpeg libjpeg-turbo libstdc++ tzdata ca-certificates
# proot fakes hard links, which uv's cache linking can't cope with; copy instead.
export UV_LINK_MODE=copy
rm -rf /opt/homeassistant /root/.cache/uv
uv venv --python /usr/bin/python3 /opt/homeassistant
uv pip install --python /opt/homeassistant/bin/python --index-strategy unsafe-best-match --extra-index-url https://wheels.home-assistant.io/musllinux-index/ homeassistant
mkdir -p /var/lib/homeassistant

name: Immich
description: Photo and video backup with the Immich phone apps. Face and object recognition are off: too heavy for phones.

name: AdGuard Home
description: Network-wide ad and tracker blocking. DNS on port 1053; devices on your tailnet can use the phone as their DNS server directly. Blocklists, statistics and a query log in its web UI.
install:
apk add --no-cache adguardhome apache2-utils
mkdir -p /var/lib/adguardhome
# Only on first install, so the user's own settings are kept. An app can't listen below
# port 1024: plain DNS is on 1053 (Tailscale devices reach it on 53, see Tailscale.kt) and
# encrypted DNS, once set up, on 8443 (DoH) and 8853 (DoT). All clients may arrive from one
# address (the router or the Tailscale relay), so there is no per-client rate limit.
if [ ! -e /var/lib/adguardhome/AdGuardHome.yaml ]; then
  pw=$(tr -dc A-Za-z0-9 < /dev/urandom | head -c 16)
  printf '%s' "$pw" > /var/lib/adguardhome/.initial-password
  hash=$(htpasswd -nbB -C 10 admin "$pw" | cut -d: -f2-)
  cat > /var/lib/adguardhome/AdGuardHome.yaml <<YAML
http:
  address: 0.0.0.0:3000
  session_ttl: 720h
users:
  - name: admin
    password: '$hash'
auth_attempts: 5
block_auth_min: 15
dns:
  bind_hosts:
    - 0.0.0.0
  port: 1053
  upstream_dns:
    - https://dns.quad9.net/dns-query
    - https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query
  bootstrap_dns:
    - 9.9.9.9
    - 1.1.1.1
  ratelimit: 0
tls:
  enabled: false
  port_https: 8443
  port_dns_over_tls: 8853
  port_dns_over_quic: 8853
filters:
  - enabled: true
    url: https://adguardteam.github.io/HostlistsRegistry/assets/filter_1.txt
    name: AdGuard DNS filter
    id: 1
  - enabled: true
    url: https://adguardteam.github.io/HostlistsRegistry/assets/filter_2.txt
    name: AdAway Default Blocklist
    id: 2
dhcp:
  enabled: false
schema_version: 29
YAML
fi

notice.text: Web UI login: admin / $1 · DNS on port 1053; open the setup guide to point your devices at it

name: Jellyseerr

name: Prowlarr
description: Indexer manager for Radarr and Sonarr. Connect your torrent tracker accounts here once; Prowlarr feeds them to Radarr and Sonarr automatically. Set up after installing Radarr and Sonarr.
install:
VER=2.7.0.5723
apk add --no-cache wget tar ca-certificates libstdc++ libgcc icu-libs sqlite-libs
case "$(apk --print-arch)" in
  aarch64) ARCH=arm64 ;;
  armv7)   ARCH=arm ;;
  x86_64)  ARCH=x64 ;;
  *) echo "Prowlarr has no build for this CPU"; exit 1 ;;
esac
if [ "$(cat /usr/local/share/prowlarr.version 2>/dev/null)" != "$VER" ]; then
  mkdir -p /tmp/prowlarr-dl
  wget -q -O /tmp/prowlarr-dl/prowlarr.tar.gz \
    "https://github.com/Prowlarr/Prowlarr/releases/download/v$VER/Prowlarr.master.$VER.linux-musl-core-$ARCH.tar.gz" \
    || { echo "Prowlarr download failed"; rm -rf /tmp/prowlarr-dl; exit 1; }
  tar -xzf /tmp/prowlarr-dl/prowlarr.tar.gz -C /tmp/prowlarr-dl
  rm -rf /opt/Prowlarr
  mv /tmp/prowlarr-dl/Prowlarr /opt/Prowlarr
  chmod +x /opt/Prowlarr/Prowlarr
  rm -rf /tmp/prowlarr-dl
  printf '%s' "$VER" > /usr/local/share/prowlarr.version
fi
mkdir -p /var/lib/prowlarr

name: Mail server (Stalwart)
description: Your own email: SMTP, IMAP and JMAP with a web admin. Open Mail in the dashboard for the setup wizard, the DNS records to add and the settings for your mail apps. Home internet connections often block port 25; read the mail guide first.
install:
# Stalwart's static musl builds from GitHub, pinned and checked against their SHA-256 (Alpine 3.24
# has no stalwart package). Stalwart 1.x keeps its settings in its database, so the stalwart-cli
# tool is installed too: the launcher uses it to apply the settings the Mail page writes.
VER=1.2.0
CLI_VER=2.0.0
apk add --no-cache xz ca-certificates
case "$(apk --print-arch)" in
  aarch64) T=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl; SW=ed8bb4ecac22a27c4d62793666cb98a51d6a63a86f65170878a9833cb9becc47
           CT=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl; CS=ded63418b83e0d38369b8adf286536cbc83701fc7e5876f0e81717e4f76ae8c7 ;;
  armv7)   T=armv7-unknown-linux-musleabihf; SW=4bee3ef463ac541596197e84e0f73f34996a59cfae8f23b6b6ea8d05c3f74b14
           CT=armv7-unknown-linux-musleabihf; CS=ea487effa4b53523a87b8f446664a7e2d30fed7e78abc3f99a7b004b3a8a56dd ;;
  x86_64)  T=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl; SW=200090ad18ea47e7633ca02f6c90e78abaff3f0028227887d48a783d04865410
           CT=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl; CS=25ab98bd38a79f1a6cd73db9a1f143807211a47f11142303cb422f2ab85f7f9e ;;
  *) echo "Stalwart has no build for this CPU"; exit 1 ;;
esac
fetch() {
  wget -q -O "$2" "$1" || { echo "Download failed: $1"; rm -f "$2"; exit 1; }
  echo "$3  $2" | sha256sum -c - >/dev/null || { echo "Checksum mismatch for $1"; rm -f "$2"; exit 1; }
}
if [ "$(cat /usr/local/share/stalwart.version 2>/dev/null)" != "$VER/$CLI_VER" ]; then
  mkdir -p /tmp/stalwart-dl /usr/local/bin /usr/local/share
  cd /tmp/stalwart-dl
  fetch "https://github.com/stalwartlabs/stalwart/releases/download/v$VER/stalwart-$T.tar.gz" stalwart.tgz "$SW"
  fetch "https://github.com/stalwartlabs/cli/releases/download/v$CLI_VER/stalwart-cli-$CT.tar.xz" cli.txz "$CS"
  tar xzf stalwart.tgz stalwart
  xz -dc cli.txz | tar x
  cp stalwart /usr/local/bin/stalwart.new
  cp "stalwart-cli-$CT/stalwart-cli" /usr/local/bin/stalwart-cli.new
  chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/stalwart.new /usr/local/bin/stalwart-cli.new
  mv /usr/local/bin/stalwart.new /usr/local/bin/stalwart
  mv /usr/local/bin/stalwart-cli.new /usr/local/bin/stalwart-cli
  printf '%s' "$VER/$CLI_VER" > /usr/local/share/stalwart.version
  cd /
  rm -rf /tmp/stalwart-dl
fi
mkdir -p /var/lib/stalwart
cat > /usr/local/bin/homedroid-stalwart <<'SH'
#!/bin/sh
# Homedroid's launcher for Stalwart. Written by the Mail app's install script; edits are overwritten.
# Setup files come from the Mail page: setup/bootstrap.json (first start) and setup/plan.ndjson
# (listeners, domain, outbound route), which is re-applied whenever it changes.
D=${STALWART_DIR:-/var/lib/stalwart}
BIN=${STALWART_BIN:-/usr/local/bin/stalwart}
CLI=${STALWART_CLI:-/usr/local/bin/stalwart-cli}
RPORT=${STALWART_RECOVERY_PORT:-8799}
CONF=$D/etc/config.json
mkdir -p "$D/etc" "$D/data" "$D/setup"
export TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS=${TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS:-2}

if [ ! -f "$D/setup/bootstrap.json" ]; then
  echo "Mail server is installed but not set up yet. Open Mail in the dashboard to set up your domain."
  while [ ! -f "$D/setup/bootstrap.json" ]; do sleep 5; done
fi

# Starts the server on the loopback-only setup port and waits for it; $1 is the probe object.
temp_server() {
  STALWART_RECOVERY_ADMIN="admin:$TMPPW" STALWART_RECOVERY_MODE_PORT=$RPORT \
    STALWART_RECOVERY_MODE_BIND=127.0.0.1 "$@" "$BIN" --config "$CONF" &
  TMPPID=$!
  i=0
  until "$CLI" --url "http://127.0.0.1:$RPORT" --user admin --password "$TMPPW" get "$PROBE" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
    i=$((i + 1))
    if [ $i -gt 90 ] || ! kill -0 "$TMPPID" 2>/dev/null; then echo "Setup server did not start"; return 1; fi
    sleep 1
  done
}
stop_temp() { kill "$TMPPID" 2>/dev/null; wait "$TMPPID" 2>/dev/null; }

TMPPW=$(tr -dc A-Za-z0-9 < /dev/urandom | head -c 24)

if [ ! -f "$CONF" ]; then
  echo "First start: creating the mail server's database…"
  PROBE=Bootstrap
  temp_server env || exit 1
  out=$("$CLI" --url "http://127.0.0.1:$RPORT" --user admin --password "$TMPPW" --no-color \
    update Bootstrap --file "$D/setup/bootstrap.json" 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  stop_temp
  user=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *username: "\(.*\)"$/\1/p')
  pass=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *secret: "\(.*\)"$/\1/p')
  if [ $rc -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$pass" ] || [ ! -f "$CONF" ]; then
    echo "Setup failed: $out"
    rm -f "$CONF"
    exit 1
  fi
  umask 077
  printf '%s' "$user" > "$D/admin-user"
  printf '%s' "$pass" > "$D/admin-password"
fi

if [ -f "$D/setup/plan.ndjson" ]; then
  want=$(sha256sum "$D/setup/plan.ndjson" | cut -d' ' -f1)
  if [ "$(cat "$D/etc/.plan-applied" 2>/dev/null)" != "$want" ]; then
    echo "Applying mail settings…"
    PROBE=SystemSettings
    temp_server env STALWART_RECOVERY_MODE=1 || exit 1
    "$CLI" --url "http://127.0.0.1:$RPORT" --user admin --password "$TMPPW" --no-color \
      apply --file "$D/setup/plan.ndjson" 2>&1
    rc=$?
    stop_temp
    if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then echo "Applying the mail settings failed"; exit 1; fi
    printf '%s' "$want" > "$D/etc/.plan-applied"
  fi
fi

echo "Mail admin login: $(cat "$D/admin-user") / $(cat "$D/admin-password")"
exec "$BIN" --config "$CONF"
SH
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/homedroid-stalwart

notice.text: Web admin login: $1 · open Mail in the dashboard for DNS records and mail app settings
